admitCard.where: Your candidate login on iimcat.ac.in, with the user ID and password created at registration. No hard copy is posted.
admitCard.when: The official CAT portal schedules admit-card downloads from 4 November 2026 for the 29 November test. As of 21 October, this is a future date; check the portal for actual availability and any later change.
steps: Keep the user ID and password from your iimcat.ac.in registration safe; you need them for everything that follows.
When the admit card link opens, sign in and download the admit card.
Check the test city, centre address, slot (session) and reporting time printed on it. You cannot choose your slot; the conducting IIM allocates the city and session.
Print it clearly. If any detail is wrong, contact the CAT helpdesk at once, before exam day.
Keep the same login handy after the exam for the response sheet, answer key and result.
carry: A printed admit card. E-copies on a phone are not accepted.
One original photo ID whose name and date of birth match your registration: Aadhaar, PAN, passport, driving licence or voter ID
Nothing else. Phones, physical calculators, watches, bags and study material are banned; rough sheets are given at the centre
admitCard.note: The test lasts 120 minutes with 40 minutes locked per section in fixed order VARC, DILR and QA; you cannot move between sections or bank time. PwD candidates get extra time.

answerKey.summary: CAT publishes every candidate's response sheet and the provisional answer key on iimcat.ac.in, usually within one to two weeks of the exam, with a paid objection window (CAT 2025: key on 4 December 2025, objections open 8 to 10 December, final key on 17 December).
steps: Sign in to iimcat.ac.in when the response sheet and provisional key are released.
Download your response sheet and compare it with the provisional key, question by question.
To challenge an answer, open the objection form, select the question, give a written justification and pay the per-question fee online before the window closes.
The conducting IIM reviews the objections and publishes the final answer key; the result is built on the final key, and accepted objections are typically refunded.
answerKey.fee: ₹1,200 per question in CAT 2025. The exact fee and window for the current cycle are announced with the key on iimcat.ac.in, so check the notice before paying.
answerKey.note: Each slot has a different paper, so the key is released per slot and raw scores are later scaled across slots before percentiles.

result.summary: The result is published on iimcat.ac.in as section-wise scaled scores and percentiles, with raw scores equated across the three slots before percentile conversion. Recent results came three to five weeks after the exam (CAT 2025: 24 December 2025; CAT 2024: 19 December 2024).

stages.what: Released on the portal one to two weeks after the exam, with a paid objection window before the final key.
Section-wise scaled scores and percentiles on iimcat.ac.in, typically in December. Download and save the scorecard within the announced window.

The percentile is only the entry ticket. Each institute publishes its own admission policy and builds shortlists on a composite of the CAT percentile (with overall and sectional minimums), Class 10, 12 and graduation marks, work experience and diversity factors, then runs a Written Ability Test or Group Discussion and a Personal Interview. Most newer IIMs share the CAP (Common Admission Process) WAT-PI round, while the older IIMs and other CAT-accepting colleges run their own. Shortlists, interviews and offers run roughly December to April on each institute's own schedule.

result.scorecard: Download the scorecard from iimcat.ac.in within the announced window and save it. A CAT score is valid for one admission cycle only, and institutes receive the scores directly through the portal, so you never send copies yourself.
